step2_answer: ANSWER: The Citation Sheet sources reviewed contain no provision requiring BWSSB to prepare its water supply or sewerage plans or schemes in coordination with the city government (the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) or the City Corporations). They provide no ULG approval or concurrence of BWSSB plans, no joint preparation and no mandatory BWSSB-to-ULG consultation. The documented links are indirect. It also prepares the master plan and infrastructure plans, and may give planning tasks to public authorities, who are then bound to assist. (ii) On BWSSB's side, there is an advisory Consultative Committee. Some of its members are appointed after consultation with bodies that represent the 'Municipal Corporation of the City of Bangalore' (the predecessor body). It advises the Board on major policy and major schemes. (iii) BWSSB schemes costing over Rs 1 crore need State Government approval, not city government approval. | EVIDENCE: BWSSB side, Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1964 (BWSSB-04, FAOLEX copy): s.15(2)(b)-(c) gives the Board the duty of 'preparing and carrying out schemes' for water supply and sewerage. Under s.62A(3) the Appellate Authority 'shall' hear both parties and pass orders. This covers tax disputes only. s.63 (Revision): the Government 'may call for the records of any proceedings of the Authority ... and may pass such order ... as it thinks fit'. This is discretionary state oversight, not a citizen channel. s.17(5) and s.18(1): affected owners are served notice to show cause, and the Authority considers 'representations, if any' before sending a scheme for sanction.
